clue.text: Aphrodisiac making old artist unsteady

indicators.note: the old one is made into the artist: one abbreviation is swapped out for another inside the word

blocks.note: an aphrodisiac is something erotic, sexually arousing
O is the standard abbreviation for old
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A love potion that leaves an elderly painter wobbly on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In EROTIC the O for old becomes RA for artist, giving ERRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable, a close synonym of unsteady.

clue.text: Very busy wanting hospital to hold operation in abnormal place

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the named letter is taken away
to hold is to keep inside, so the word wraps around the inserted letters

blocks.note: hectic means frantically busy
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A frantic hospital without beds has to fit in an operation somewhere unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: HECTIC loses its H to give ECTIC, which then holds OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectopic is a medical term for something occurring out of its normal position, as in an ectopic pregnancy.

clue.text: Prisoner ultimately given sentence – possibly raised in case of firearm

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
something possibly stirred up is disturbed, so these letters may be shaken into another order

blocks.note: the last letter
a life sentence, the longest a prisoner can get

explanation.surface: A convict's life sentence might be increased because a gun was involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like sentencing law: a firearm offence raising the term. Here 'possibly raised' tells us to rearrange the letters of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun, a particular kind of firearm.

clue.text: At the end Alistair Darling introduces finance officer

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of the following name
something that introduces another comes first, so these pieces stand in front

blocks.note: darling and treasure are both terms of endearment
the last letter

explanation.surface: Alistair Darling, Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, was a finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Alistair Darling was the UK's Chancellor, its finance minister, so the name looks like the definition; it is split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer who manages the funds of a club, company or government.

clue.text: Tea dance, 50% off

indicators.note: half off means the word loses one of its two equal halves

blocks.note: the cha-cha is a Latin American dance

explanation.surface: An afternoon tea dance with a half-price sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea dance' reads as one event, but tea is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is an informal British word for tea, borrowed from Chinese.

clue.text: Jump leads to start all Leyland cars – that follows

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept
follows tells us this word is placed after the letters already built

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words
how can be used as a conjunction meaning that, as in 'he told me how he had been ill'

explanation.surface: Instructions for jump-starting a fleet of old British Leyland cars with jump leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jump leads' looks like a single motoring phrase, but jump is the definition and leads the selection signal. British Leyland was a UK car maker of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating jump, taking off from the back inside edge of one skate.

clue.text: Detectives turned up for drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: PIs are private investigators

explanation.surface: Police investigators arrive for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sip is a small mouthful of a drink, and to sip is to drink slowly.

clue.text: Shelter beside church drain

indicators.note: beside means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A sheltered spot next to a church where the rainwater drains.
explanation.definitionFit: To leech is to drain someone, as a bloodsucking leech does, so it means to exhaust their resources.

clue.text: Actor on series gets hamper

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer
a string is a series, as in a string of hits

explanation.surface: A performer in a TV series receives a gift basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamper looks like a picnic basket noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple or obstruct them, a vivid synonym of hamper as a verb.

clue.text: Cast Lloyd Bridges right after western knowing ...

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the letters of the name are tossed into a new arrangement
something that bridges spans across another, so it wraps around the inserted letter
after means following, so this part comes later than the letter it follows

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Lloyd Bridges, the American actor, was cast in the right western role.
explanation.walkthrough: Lloyd Bridges was a Hollywood actor, so his surname looks like part of a name; it is the container signal. The ellipsis runs on into 12 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly means experienced and sophisticated, knowing in the ways of the world.

clue.text: Fair provision of internet service provider and phone company used by aristocrat?

indicators.note: what is used by someone comes after them, so these pieces follow the person's word

blocks.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class person
EE is a British mobile and broadband company
Apple makes the iPhone

explanation.surface: A question about which broadband and phone firms a posh person signs up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the aristocrat is a toff, British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: A toffee apple is a sweet treat sold at fairgrounds, an apple on a stick coated in hard toffee.

clue.text: Spoil drive back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word from its end to its start

blocks.note: to ram is to drive or force something in

explanation.surface: A short instruction about ruining a driveway or a trip home.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or blemish it, a synonym of spoil.

clue.text: Leaned on print media journalist after you are caught

indicators.note: something caught is held fast inside, so these letters sit within the others

blocks.note: the press is newspapers and magazines
ED is short for editor
text-speak shorthand for you are

explanation.surface: A reporter bullies someone who has been caught out by the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: UR is text-speak for 'you are'. 'Caught' signals that the other pieces hold it inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be leaned on is to be put under pressure or coerced, an idiom matching pressured.

clue.text: ... direction spoken by pro will get support

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the one meant

blocks.note: a route is a direction to take, and many speakers say it to rhyme with boot
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Continuing 8 down: a savvy professional backs the right instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 8 down for the surface only; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To root for someone is an idiom meaning to cheer them on and back them.

clue.text: Despicable sort's boring phone having numbered display

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person
to dial is to phone someone

explanation.surface: A tedious person keeps talking about their phone, which has a number screen.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for an unpleasant person; it bores into DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital clock or meter shows readings as digits rather than with hands on a dial.

clue.text: Loathed pitching the ad

indicators.note: pitching suggests tossing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone detested having to sell an advertising campaign to a client.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathed and hated are both past tenses of verbs for intense dislike.

clue.text: Meeting place with solemnity providing focus for mass

blocks.note: a centre is a place where people gather, as in a community centre
of can mean having, as in a man of courage
gravity is seriousness of manner

explanation.surface: A church hall where a solemn Mass is held.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks religious after meeting place and solemnity, but it is the physics sense: weight.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics the centre of gravity is the point where an object's weight acts, the focal point of its mass.

clue.text: National park in N-Nottingham?

blocks.note: surface reading: a stammered question about a national park somewhere near Nottingham
setter's reading: N is short for new, and the football club Nottingham ___ is completed by the second word of the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club; put N for new in front of Nottingham and the club becomes a national park in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a national park in southern England, an ancient royal hunting ground of heath and woodland.

clue.text: Extremely deficient paper breaks up leaving holes

indicators.note: lacking at the extremes means the outer letters go and the middle is kept
leaving means departing, so the named letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
ruptures are breaks or bursts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor-quality paper falls apart and is left full of tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks up' reads as a phrasal verb, but up is the piece that leaves RUPTURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are openings or gaps, so they are a synonym of holes.

clue.text: Stable reliable sort in AA – perhaps owing to resolution

blocks.note: the AA, Britain's Automobile Association, tows broken-down cars, so it is a tower, one that tows
of can mean because of, as in die of hunger
resolution is strength of will

explanation.surface: A dependable motorist's organisation sticks to its resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown service; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for a person you can rely on for support in difficult times.

clue.text: Wanted to play with guitar at the top – plucked string?

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so only the first letter is kept
letters set to play are free to move around into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A musician longed to perform on a guitar at the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Twanged describes a vibrating sound made by plucking, which the question mark ties to a guitar string.

clue.text: Somebody once discovered Chase buzzer's broken at the base

indicators.note: dis-covered means its cover stripped away, so the outer letters go
in a down entry the base is the bottom, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
a bee buzzes; the 's just joins the pieces
the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone found that the buzzer on the TV quiz The Chase has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chase is a British TV quiz show, so Chase and buzzer seem to belong together; 'discovered' means uncovered, not found.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person who was once famous or important but no longer is.

clue.text: Sidestep in rally round about 15 love

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word wraps around the inner letters

blocks.note: to rally round is to help, give aid
the answer to 15 across is centre of gravity, read literally as the central letter of the word gravity
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A tennis player dodges a shot during a rally at fifteen-love.
explanation.walkthrough: '15 love' reads as a tennis score, but 15 points to 15 across, CENTRE OF GRAVITY: the centre of gravity is V. AID goes around V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to sidestep it, dodging rather than facing it.

clue.text: Divine party with someone on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside is cleared and only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: a do is a party
W is the abbreviation for with
only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A heavenly party with a friend while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Divine looks like an adjective, heavenly; it is the verb, to search for water.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water with a rod, which is also called divining.

clue.text: How's your father, mother, uncle and aunt?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for sex
second meaning: family members

explanation.surface: A polite enquiry about the health of the whole family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is jocular British slang for sexual activity, so the question is really two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations means both sexual intercourse and family kin, and the clue gives one phrase for each sense.

clue.text: Cow maybe dropping head like a sheep

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is removed

blocks.note: a cow is an example of a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A cow lowering its head looks rather like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine is the adjective for sheep, from the Latin ovis.

clue.text: Source of green energy set to be unlimited – wow!

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept
without limits means losing its boundaries, so the end letters are dropped and the middle kept

blocks.note: the first letter
E is the physics symbol for energy
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Renewable power is about to become limitless, which is exciting news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of green energy' reads as one phrase, and indeed it defines 25 across, but here it is split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is an informal exclamation of surprise or enthusiasm, like wow.

clue.text: Source of green energy wired in but not initially working

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it qualifies
working means being worked on, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A power source has been connected up but isn't yet running.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind turbine generates electricity from moving air, a renewable kind of power.

clue.text: Vote of American in New York

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: An American casts a ballot in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old word for no, used when voting against a motion.

clue.text: Best pan on the counter

indicators.note: counter means running against, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a pot is a cooking pan

explanation.surface: The finest saucepan sits on the kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: The counter looks like a kitchen worktop; it means against, and in a down entry the word runs upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Top as an adjective means best or highest-ranking, as in top marks.

clue.text: Indecisive writing journal – change article to be definite

indicators.note: turning the indefinite article into the definite one means swapping one small word for another

blocks.note: a diary is a journal written in daily
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone who can't make up their mind about what to put in their diary.
explanation.walkthrough: In DIARY the indefinite article A is replaced by the definite article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone who hesitates and can't make up their mind, so it is a synonym of indecisive.

clue.text: Bill Nighy's opening door

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: a bill is a printed notice stuck on a wall, as in billboard
the first letter

explanation.surface: Actor Bill Nighy is starring in a new production on its opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Nighy is a British actor, so Bill reads as a first name; here it is a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small back or side door, especially one in a castle wall.
